problem_text:
Study the examples and non-examples of bases and heights in a triangle. Answer the questions that follow.
- These dashed segments represent heights of the triangle.
[image]
- These dashed segments do not represent heights of the triangle.
[image]
Select all the statements that are true about bases and heights in a triangle.

Answer choices:
A. Any side of a triangle can be a base. || There is only one possible height. || A height is always one of the sides of a triangle. || A height that corresponds to a base must be drawn at an acute angle to the base. || A height that corresponds to a base must be drawn at a right angle to the base. || Once we choose a base
B. there is only one segment that represents the corresponding height. || A segment representing a height must go through a vertex.
